target_customer: Indian consumers (home collection and labs), hospitals and other labs for outsourced testing
problem: Diagnostic testing in India is fragmented and slow; Redcliffe offers a wide test menu with home collection and same day reports.
business_model: Diagnostics services revenue per test, omnichannel labs, collection centres and home collection
product_category: Diagnostics and pathology labs, digital health

founders.name: Dheeraj Jain
previous_startups: women's health D2C company (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: about 15 years in corporate strategy and M&A with buyout experience, 5 years early stage investing.

founders.name: Aditya Kandoi
previous_startups: earlier health-tech ventures (unnamed on YC page)
founders.background_notes: Health consulting roles per YC page.

competitors.traction_then: AIIMS and Dr Lal PathLabs named as Redcliffe clients

competitors.name: Orange Health
competitors.what: on-demand home sample collection startup founded 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly lab operations, logistics and quality accreditation rather than software; genetic and specialised testing add technical depth.

defensibility.rationale: Owned labs and collection networks (30 plus labs, 700 plus centres per the YC description) and accreditation take capital and time to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not buy Redcliffe by 2026; it raised 61 million Series B in 2022 and 42 million Series C in 2024 and made its own acquisitions (Celara, Megavision).

market_need_then: Large unmet diagnostic demand in India and Covid 19 shifted testing to home collection; the YC description claims millions served and 250K plus parameters daily.

identity.voice_and_tone: consumer health, tagline Healthy India Ki Trusted Lab per a directory

rebrands.why: not sourced; one directory only, unverified

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage of the drone corridor from Uttarkashi to Dehradun in the company description; no merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Consumer brand across 120 plus cities per the YC description and covered by Indian business press, but no evidence the brand itself drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Redcliffe built owned labs and home collection in India, joined YC in Winter 2021, then raised a 61 million Series B in May 2022 and a 42 million Series C in September 2024. It has grown through acquisitions and in April 2026 sold its fertility unit Crysta IVF to refocus on diagnostics. Growth is tied to a large market, the Covid era shift to home testing and capital for lab expansion.
